text: Debugging is an essential skill for any programmer. When your code doesn't work, the first step is identifying the bug. This means understanding the problem—is it a simple typo, a logic error, or something more complex? Instead of guessing, take a systematic approach. Try to isolate the issue by testing small parts of your code independently. Modern debugging tools, like breakpoints and step-through features, are incredibly helpful. They let you pause the program and inspect its state at any moment. Another powerful technique is logging. By adding print statements or using a logger, you can track the flow of data and see exactly where things go wrong. Remember, patience is key; a clear method beats random tinkering every time.
